fixes.explanation: Hold on, friend. Jude says the faith was entrusted “…once for all to the saints.” That leaves no room for a new version every time somebody new takes the microphone. He tells them to contend for it, not rewrite it.
Fasting isn't in this verse, friend. Jude says they turn the grace of our God into “…a license for immorality…” These men are using grace to give themselves permission, not to hold anything back.

That's the word. Jude says Sodom and Gomorrah “…are on display as an example of those who sustain the punishment of eternal fire.” They're held up like a warning sign by the road. Jude puts them on display on purpose.

No armies in this verse, friend. Jude says these men, “…like irrational animals…” will be destroyed “…by the things they do instinctively.” The things they do are what destroy them. Nobody has to draw a sword.
Yes. Jude calls them “fruitless trees in autumn, twice dead after being uprooted.” No fruit, and uprooted, that's the picture. It's a rough image, so I'll leave it there.

I get why a star would tempt you to say that. But Jude says these wandering stars have “blackest darkness” reserved for them. The word he uses is darkness, and he says it's reserved “forever.” That one's heavy, so I'll leave it there.

That's the opposite of what Jude says, friend. He says these wandering stars have “blackest darkness” reserved for them “forever.” The word he uses is darkness, not light. Nothing in that verse says they get a light of their own.
Right. Enoch prophesied, “Behold, the Lord is coming with myriads of His holy ones…” Enoch is the seventh from Adam, and Jude says he prophesied about these men. The one coming is the Lord.
Jude doesn't say that, friend. His words are, “And indeed, have mercy on those who doubt…” The instruction is mercy, not keeping away.

That's right. Jude says God is able “…to present you unblemished in His glorious presence, with great joy…” Unblemished, in His glorious presence, with great joy. That's what he says God is able to do.

Yes. Jude writes, “…to the only God our Savior be glory, majesty, dominion, and authority through Jesus Christ our Lord before all time, and now, and for all eternity.” Before all time, now, and for all eternity. That's the closing, right there in verse 25.
